# Claude Code approval-card byte verification

Captured live from `claude` v2.1.185 on 2026-06-23 by driving an interactive
session in a PTY and triggering a Bash tool-approval prompt (probe command:
`echo PROBE-$RANDOM-$(date +%s)`). Locks `APPROVE_BYTES` / `DENY_BYTES` in
`crates/app/src/shell/approval_card.rs`.

## Approve = b"1\r"   (0x31 0x0d)

The menu always lists "Yes" as option 1, pre-highlighted (the `❯` cursor sits
on it). Pressing `1` selects it; the trailing CR (raw-mode Enter) confirms.
Holds for both the 2-option and 3-option menu shapes.

## Deny = b"\x1b"   (Esc)

Pressing `Esc` cancels the prompt regardless of how many options are shown:
the captured session printed `Interrupted · What should Claude do instead?`
and the tool was NOT run. (Esc then drops into an OPTIONAL "what should Claude
do instead?" free-text field, which the card's free-text input already feeds.)

A fixed numeric `2` is WRONG for deny — the menu shape is command-dependent:

  * command with shell expansion/substitution (cannot become an allow-rule),
    e.g. `echo $RANDOM`        ->  2 options:  `1. Yes`   `2. No`
  * simple static command (rule-able), e.g. `ls`
        ->  3 options:  `1. Yes`   `2. Yes, and don't ask again`   `3. No (esc)`

So `2` means "No" for the first but "Yes, and don't ask again" (an approve that
ALSO writes a permanent allow-rule) for the second. `Esc` is the only reliable,
universal deny.

## Captured menu (verbatim, ANSI-stripped)

    Bash command
      echo PROBE-$RANDOM-$(date +%s)
       Echo probe string with random and timestamp
    Contains simple_expansion
    Do you want to proceed?
    ❯ 1. Yes
      2. No
      Esc to cancel · Tab to amend · ctrl+e to explain

## If a future Claude Code version differs

Re-run the capture (interactive `claude` in a PTY, trigger a Bash prompt) and
update `APPROVE_BYTES` / `DENY_BYTES` + the `approve_and_deny_bytes_match_live_prompt`
test to match, noting the version range here.
